_purpose: WBS task id -> the repository evidence that proves its deliverable exists.
_why: IMP-0030: WBS 0.4 was marked Status=Done while five of the eight tables its own description names were absent from the solution, and 1.2's deliverable existed with a blank Status. A hand-typed Status column is a claim, not a result (same class as exit-zero-does-not-mean-created). scripts/derive-wbs-state.py reads this map, checks each rule against the repository, and reports every disagreement between the claim and the evidence.

_kinds.path: a file or directory that must exist (glob allowed)
_kinds.grep: {"file": glob, "pattern": regex} — pattern must match in at least one file
_kinds.manual: no repository evidence is possible; the reason is required and the task can never derive as complete from the repo alone

_unlisted_tasks: derive as status 'unknown' and are COUNTED AND NAMED in the report, never silently treated as complete.

No repository evidence can express it: every build gate reads what the app ASKS for and column security decides what it GETS, and only a signed-in trustee separates those. The two path rules below evidence the SHARE half of 'Shared app + access test'; this rule is the test half, which read complete on file existence alone across three evidence-map revisions (improvement review 18, IMP-0230, IMP-0067)

8.2._note: REWRITTEN 2026-09-09 (pm-agent, IMP-0675). The previous two rules were an entity rule for rev_bankaccount - which is 8.1's evidence, so 8.2 rode on 8.1 - and a grep for the bare string 'rev_bankaccount' across src/solutions/*/Roles/*/*.xml. That grep matched an XML COMMENT in REV Trustee.xml saying the Trustee role has NO privilege on that table, i.e. the OPPOSITE of the deliverable, and also matched REV Service Automation's app-user privileges, which are not the finance role either. 8.2's deliverable is the REV Finance security role: no Roles/REV Finance/ directory exists, and the REV_FinanceOnly column-security profile that is built has no member wired to it. Rules below name that role's own file and the GRANTED RolePrivilege elements inside it, so no comment and no other role can satisfy them. Same class as the 2026-08-19 tightening _rule_quality_note already records for this task - the tightening regressed.

8.3._note: REWRITTEN 2026-09-09 (pm-agent, per TAD rev 6 §9.4.1). The previous single rule was a directory-existence check on AppModules/rev_financecapture — the ADR-044 separate app, which the reviewer rejected in rev 6, restoring the payment capture form inside the existing rev_grantadministration app. That directory will never exist, so the old rule was unsatisfiable and 8.3 could never derive complete, which is worse than a weak rule. The five rules below name one file and one granted element each: two AppModuleComponent greps and two SubArea greps (the app-designer half and the runtime-render half, for both secured tables), plus a FormXml/main path check that is the one rule a comment cannot satisfy, per TAD §9.4.1's rationale. EXTENDED 2026-09-10 (pm-agent, IMP-0705): those five rules are correct about WHAT the deliverable is and wrong about WHAT LEVEL proves it — all five are source-existence checks, i.e. V1, and both governing documents forbid reporting this task complete even on V3. Three rules were added after them so the rule set is a V-level ladder rather than five instances of one level: a build-manifest rule (V2), a pipeline-log import rule (V3), and a manual rule for the V4 sign-off that no repository artefact can ever evidence. Nothing was loosened; the five original rules still all have to pass.

V2 (packaged). Added 2026-09-10 (IMP-0705). Rules 1-5 above are all source-existence checks: every one of them is satisfied by V1 well-formed source, so the five together derived `complete` for a task whose approved design (TAD ADR-047, SDD section 8 D-1) forbids reporting complete even on V3. This rule requires a build manifest that names wbs 8.3 AND records status SUCCESS in the SAME file - the two halves are one regex on purpose, so a successful build of some other task cannot supply the second half. build/artifacts/** is gitignored EXCEPT manifest.json (see .gitignore), so this is checkable from committed artifacts on a fresh clone.

V3 (accepted by a target). Added 2026-09-10 (IMP-0705). This is the repository's established V3 evidence path - skills/how-to-verify-a-platform-contract.md section 5: 'Before writing V3 anywhere, grep logs/pipeline.log for an actual import/deploy entry naming THIS build's content.' A build manifest's own verification_level field is a claim, never the evidence, which is why the rule above asserts only SUCCESS and this one asserts the import. The wbs: list is matched inside the log line's own trailing tag so a V3 success for a different task cannot satisfy it; asserted negative 2026-09-10 - the identical pattern with 3.3 substituted DOES match, 8.3 does not, because this build has never been imported.

8.3.reason: V4 sign-off: a signed-in REV Finance user opens the payment capture form and sees data. TAD ADR-047 and SDD section 8 D-1 both state that wbs:8.3 must not be reported complete on V3 evidence, and TAD section 6.2.1's level-by-level table records V4 as blocked by two independent causes until wbs:8.2 delivers the REV Finance role - share-apps.ps1 grants app access by role NAME and fails when the role is absent, and with no member in REV_FinanceOnly every one of the 16 secured columns across rev_bankaccount and rev_payment renders empty for every user, including the form's author. No repository artefact can observe a person opening a form, so this rule can never be satisfied here: it caps wbs:8.3 at complete_pending_manual until a dated V4 confirmation is recorded. NOTE FOR THE READER OF logs/state/wbs-state.json: contract/delivery-parameters.json's complete_states currently INCLUDES complete_pending_manual, so that state still clears successors and still counts as complete for invoicing - see the finding logged against this rule.

_rule_quality_note: A rule must be satisfiable only by the deliverable existing, never by a declaration that it will. 8.2 and 6.5 initially passed on a role privilege naming a table that did not exist and on a generic provisioning script — both were tightened on 2026-08-19. Same class as gate-cannot-fail: a rule that cannot fail is not a check. 8.2 REGRESSED and was rewritten again on 2026-09-09 (IMP-0675): it had drifted back to an entity rule belonging to 8.1 plus a bare-string grep across every role file, which matched an XML COMMENT stating the Trustee role has NO privilege on the table - the rule passed on the negation of its own deliverable. A tightening is not durable unless the rule NAMES THE ARTEFACT: prefer a rule pointing at one specific file and one specific granted element over a glob and a substring, because a glob widens every time a sibling file is added. 8.3 was also corrected on 2026-09-09 (TAD rev 6 §9.4.1): its prior rule checked for the ADR-044 separate app directory, which the reviewer rejected — an unsatisfiable rule, worse than a weak one, since the task could never derive complete. Replaced with five rules naming one file and one granted element each: two AppModuleComponent greps, two SubArea greps, and a FormXml/main path check, none of which the pre-existing repository state satisfies. THIRD CORRECTION, 2026-09-10 (IMP-0705): a rule set can name the right artefact and still be wrong, by proving too EARLY a stage of it. All five 8.3 rules were source-existence checks — V1 — and 8.3 derived complete the day its source was authored, while TAD ADR-047 and SDD §8 D-1 both say in terms that it must not be reported complete even on V3. So the shape rule has a second half: a rule set must reach the LEVEL its governing design requires, not merely name the deliverable. Where the required level is repo-checkable, add a rule at that level (a build manifest for V2, a logs/pipeline.log import entry for V3); where it is not — a human opening the thing, a client accepting it — add a `manual` rule so the task caps at complete_pending_manual instead of reading complete. Ask of any rule set: what is the HIGHEST level every one of these rules is satisfied by, and is that the level the design asks for?
